subject: Geopolitics
title: Containment Strategy
description: A short lesson to help you apply Containment Strategy.

hook.text: The US didn't try to destroy the USSR. It built a fence around it and waited for it to rot from inside.

buildup.text: Containment meant alliances (NATO), aid (Marshall Plan), and military bases ringing the Soviet bloc.

discovery.text: The strategy assumed communism would fail if it couldn't expand. Keep it boxed and time does the work.

twist.text: Containment was expensive. Korea, Vietnam, and dozens of covert ops cost trillions and millions of lives.

climax.text: Yet it worked on its own terms. By 1991 the USSR collapsed without a direct US–Soviet war.

punchline.text: Patience can be a weapon sharper than any missile.

quiz.question: What was the core assumption behind containment?
options: The USSR would attack first if provoked
Communism would fail if it could not expand
Nuclear war was inevitable within a decade
